points.description: States the verdict FALSE for the statement that processes of the same program share one PCB with a reference counter.
Justifies that each process is an independent entity that needs its own separate OS state (its own PCB) to track its execution.
points.partial_credit: Half (0.25) if it says processes are independent but does not say each needs its own separate state or PCB.

points.description: Names the per-process state that must be kept separate: execution memory contents, open files, memory allocations and stack state.
points.partial_credit: Half (0.25) if at least two of the four named items (memory contents, open files, memory allocations, stack state) are stated correctly.

points.description: States that a single shared PCB cannot provide this separate per-process state, so the reference-counter idea is wrong.
points.partial_credit: Half (0.25) if it says a shared PCB is wrong but gives no reason tied to separate per-process state.

rubric.notes: Full marks (2) need FALSE plus a justification that each process is independent and needs its own separate OS state, naming the state (memory contents, open files, memory allocations, stack state), and stating that one shared PCB cannot give this. A correct verdict with no justification earns no justification marks, and any claim that processes of the same program may share a PCB or that the reference counter is valid costs the related point. Vague wording such as "each process is different" earns nothing.
